steps.content:

steps.label: Do Now: Follow the Input
steps.content:
Do Now: Follow the Input

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is the order of the input() lines important?Show the answer

The first thing typed goes into the first input(). Swap the lines and the values swap too.

From 2.2. Follow the program one line at a time.

name = input("Name? ")
age = int(input("Age? "))
print(name + " will be " + str(age + 2))
Total: 3 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: follow the input

steps.text: This is a different program. The user types Pai, then 30.
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = float(input("Temperature? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 2))

steps.text: Line 1: the first thing typed goes into city. city holds the String "Pai".
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = float(input("Temperature? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 2))
city: "Pai"

steps.text: Line 2: float() turns "30" into a number with a decimal point. temp holds 30.0, a Real.
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = float(input("Temperature? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 2))
temp: 30.0, a Real

steps.text: Line 3: work out the brackets first. temp + 2 is 32.0. str() makes it the String "32.0".
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = float(input("Temperature? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 2))
"32.0"

steps.text: Then + joins the Strings from left to right, spaces and all.
steps.visual:
city = input("City? ")
temp = float(input("Temperature? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 2))
It prints Pai is 32.0

steps.text: Now do the same with your program: write down what each variable holds, line by line.
steps.visual:

temp = float(input("Temperature? "))
print(city + " is " + str(temp + 2))

steps.label: 2.3: Programs Using Data Types
steps.content:
Text-based Programming

2.3: Programs Using Data Types

Year 7

  • Today: watch, explain, and make notes on three ideas. Then use your notes in Circuit Siege.
  • The big question: why does choosing the right data type, and the right name, matter?
Think → Pair → ShareA shop app stores your name, your phone number and the price of what you buy. Why might it store each one in a different way?Show the answer

Each value is used in a different way. Some are used for maths, some are only shown. Today we find out how to choose.

steps.label: Watch: Choose the Data Type
steps.content:
Watch: Choose the Data Type

Think → Pair → ShareBefore you watch: a phone number is made of digits. Does that make it a number? Why?Show the answer

Make a guess with your partner. Then watch to check.

steps.label: Explain It: Why a String?
steps.content:
Explain It: Why a String?

Think → Pair → ShareWhere else do you see digits that are not used for maths?Show the answer

A bus number, a room number like 12B, a PIN code. Nobody adds them up.

Explain it in your own words. Press Check my answer to have it marked.

items.context: The animation ran phone = int(input("Phone? ")) and print(phone). The user typed 0812345678. int() turned it into the Integer 812345678: a whole number never starts with 0, so the 0 at the start was lost, and print showed the wrong number. With phone = input("Phone? ") and no int(), phone held the String "0812345678" and print showed every digit. Nobody does maths with a phone number. In your own words, explain why a phone number like 0812345678 should be stored as a String, not an Integer.
items.prompt: In your own words, explain why a phone number like 0812345678 should be stored as a String, not an Integer.
scheme: The program never does maths / adds or multiplies with a phone number
As an Integer the 0 at the start is lost (812345678) / a String keeps every digit / a number cannot start with 0
items.guidance: One mark for each point, in the student's own words. "It has digits" or "it is long" alone earns nothing. Accept "it can have a + or spaces" for the second point.
items.modelAnswer: Nobody does maths with a phone number. As an Integer the 0 at the start is lost; a String keeps every digit.

Note in your notes: WHY a phone number is stored as a String.Check my note

A model note: No maths is done with it, and as an Integer it would lose the 0 at the start.

steps.label: Explain It: Why a Real, and Why str()?
steps.content:
Explain It: Why a Real, and Why str()?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a shop till show prices with a decimal point?Show the answer

Money has parts of a baht or a pound. A whole number cannot show them.

Explain it in your own words. Press Check my answer to have it marked.

items.context: The animation ran price = 2.5, count = 3, total = price * count and print("Total: " + str(total)). price held the Real 2.5 and count the Integer 3. A Real times an Integer gives a Real, so total held 7.5, a Real. + cannot join the String "Total: " to a Real, so str(total) turned it into the String "7.5", and the screen showed Total: 7.5. price is 2.5 and count is 3. In your own words, explain why total = price * count is a Real, and why the print line needs str(total).
items.prompt: price is 2.5 and count is 3. In your own words, explain why total = price * count is a Real, and why the print line needs str(total).
scheme: A Real times an Integer gives a Real / the answer 7.5 has a decimal point
+ cannot join a String and a number, so str() turns total into a String
items.guidance: One mark for each point, in the student's own words. "Because of str()" alone earns nothing: it must say + joins only text, or that the number must become text.
items.modelAnswer: A Real times an Integer gives a Real: 7.5. + can only join Strings, so str() makes total a String first.

steps.label: Your Notes: Two Data Types Together
steps.content:
Your Notes: Two Data Types Together

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is it useful to know the data type of every variable in a program?Show the answer

Then you can tell what each line will do, and where str() or int() is needed.

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top) and write each note in your own words. Then press Check my note and compare. Fix your note if it misses an idea. You will use these notes in Circuit Siege.

Note in your notes: what data type you get when an Integer and a Real meet in a sum.Check my note

A model note: A Real. One Real in the sum makes the answer a Real. / always gives a Real too.

Note in your notes: WHY str() is needed to join text and a number with +.Check my note

A model note: + can only join two Strings, so str() turns the number into a String first.

steps.label: Watch: The Same Name Every Time
steps.content:
Watch: The Same Name Every Time

Think → Pair → ShareBefore you watch: does Python care about capital letters in a name? Why might it?Show the answer

Make a guess with your partner. Then watch to check.

steps.label: Explain It: Why Did Score Stop It?
steps.content:
Explain It: Why Did Score Stop It?

Think → Pair → ShareWhere else must a name be typed exactly the same every time?Show the answer

A password, an email address, a username. One wrong letter and it does not work.

Explain it in your own words. Press Check my answer to have it marked.

items.context: The animation ran score = 5, score = score + 1 and print(Score). score held 6. Line 3 asked for Score, with a capital S. Python sees score and Score as different names, and no variable called Score was ever stored, so the program stopped with an error. print(score) showed 6. Then a typo, scroe = score + 1, made a new variable called scroe holding 6, so print(score) showed 5 with no error. In your own words, explain why print(Score) stops with an error when the program stored the value in score.
items.prompt: In your own words, explain why print(Score) stops with an error when the program stored the value in score.
scheme: Python sees capitals as different / Score and score are different names
No variable called Score was ever stored / given a value, so Python cannot find it
items.guidance: One mark for each point, in the student's own words. "It is spelt wrong" alone earns nothing: it must say the capital makes it a different name, or that Score has no value.
items.modelAnswer: Python sees Score and score as different names. Nothing was ever stored in Score, so it cannot be found.

steps.label: Your Notes: The Same Name Every Time
steps.content:
Your Notes: The Same Name Every Time

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is a spelling slip that gives no message worse than one that does?Show the answer

With a message you know there is a problem. With no message, the wrong answer can go unnoticed.

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top) and write each note in your own words. Then press Check my note and compare. Fix your note if it misses an idea. You will use these notes in Circuit Siege.

Note in your notes: WHY capital letters in a variable name matter.Check my note

A model note: Python sees score and Score as different names. Using a name that was never stored stops the program with an error.

Note in your notes: WHY a spelling slip can give a wrong answer with no error.Check my note

A model note: A new spelling, like scroe = score + 1, makes a new variable. The real one keeps its old value.
